chunks: Whoever begins speech before the greeting (al-salam), do not answer him.
And he said: Begin with the greeting before speech. So whoever begins with speech before the greeting, do not answer him.

key_terms.السَّلَامُ: The Islamic greeting of peace — 'al-salam alaykum'; here used as the obligatory ritual greeting that must precede conversation
key_terms.الْكَلَامُ: Speech, talk, conversation — any words exchanged between people
key_terms.تُجِيبُوهُ: Answer him, respond to him — the prohibition applies to engaging with one who skips the greeting

ai.seo_question: Should you respond to someone who speaks without giving the Islamic greeting first?
ai.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) teaches that initiating the Islamic greeting (al-salam) must precede any conversation. One who speaks without first offering the greeting of peace is to be met with silence — this etiquette reflects that al-salam is a right due to every Muslim, and neglecting it signals a breach of proper Islamic social conduct. In the early Muslim community, al-salam (السلام عليكم) was understood as more than a greeting; it was a covenant of peace, security, and recognition of shared faith, so to omit it was considered a social and spiritual failing.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who begins the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Initiate with the greeting (السَّلَامُ) before the speech. So the one who begins with the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “If one begins speaking before offering the greeting of peace, do not speak to him.”
